title: The Cicerone's Round
theme: Five stops through Rome in the Jubilee of 1750 with Domenico Fabbri, a cicerone who guides foreign gentlemen on the Grand Tour. Half the city is a building site, half of it is a cattle pasture with emperors buried under it, and everyone is selling something to the English.

companion.name: Domenico Fabbri
companion.brief: Forty-four, a cicerone who walks English, French and German gentlemen round the antiquities for a fee, having learned his Latin from a priest and his English from his customers. Born in Rome, near the Pantheon. Charming, mercenary, genuinely in love with the ruins he sells. He knows what every guide's fee is, which antiquities are fake, and nothing of the world after 1750.

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in Rome in 1750: baroque facades, weathered travertine, ruins overgrown with grass and shrubs, cattle and carts in the forum, scaffolding, sedan chairs, priests and travellers. Clothing of the mid eighteenth century: tricornes, breeches, cassocks, shawls. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Warm Roman light, muted colour, not sepia.
style.avoid: no nineteenth-century excavations of the forum (it is still buried and grazed), no motor vehicles, no electric light, no modern clothing, no Victor Emmanuel monument (1911), no text overlays

stops.title: Piazza di Spagna
stops.brief: The foreigners' quarter: the new steps of twenty-five years ago, lodging houses full of English travellers, artists' models waiting to be hired, and guides waiting for customers.
mustCover: who lodges here and what they pay
the steps and how new they are

stops.title: The Trevi Fountain
stops.brief: The fountain half built: the wall going up, blocks of travertine in the square, the old outlet still running, and the crowd that comes to watch the work.
mustCover: what is being built and how long it has taken
what Romans think of the expense

stops.title: The Pantheon
stops.brief: The best preserved building of the ancients, with two bell towers on the front that Romans mock, and a portico used as a market and a shelter.
mustCover: why it survived when the rest did not
the bell towers and what people call them
what a traveller is charged to be shown round

stops.title: Campo Vaccino
stops.brief: The Roman Forum as it is now: a cattle market with column tops sticking out of the earth, buffalo and cows, and diggers turning up marble for the lime kilns.
mustCover: what is buried here and how deep
what happens to the marble that is dug up

stops.title: The Colosseum
stops.brief: The amphitheatre full of wild plants and small shrines, the Stations of the Cross set up inside it last year, hermits living in the arches and stone still being carried away.
mustCover: what it is used for now
the crosses set up inside and why
